reference.title: Cable Seated Chest Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come back to the chest, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s back, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press while sitting tall without leaning back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on each stack; slower return

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench between two towers, facing away from the pulleys set about shoulder height, feet flat; a D-handle in each hand, arms extended in front of the chest, palms down.
Breathe in and let the handles come back to the sides of the chest, elbows travelling back and out at about 45-60 degrees.
Pause with the hands beside the chest and a light stretch across the chest; shoulders down.
Breathe out and press the handles forward and slightly together until the arms are long, elbows soft.
Squeeze the chest with the hands in front; stay tall without leaning back into the cables.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding forward or leaning back off the bench
mistakes.fix: Sit tall with the chest up; lighten the stacks if the cables pull you back.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to push
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, glutes tight, move only the arms.
Keep the shoulders down and back throughout.

kinematics.norm: From well bent with the hands beside the chest to nearly straight in front (clinical opinion)
About 45-60 degrees from the trunk at the chest (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms down, handles across the body (clinical opinion)
One cable per hand from its own pulley behind the athlete at about shoulder height (clinical opinion)
Sitting tall, no back support; seated presses need less trunk muscle work than standing ones (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012)
Flat bench about knee height, feet flat, knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s back and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Seated Chest Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press without being pulled backward.
Sit down with the handles one at a time (or have the stacks set so you can reach them from the bench); at the end of the set bring the hands back to the chest before letting the handles go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: sit with the back against an upright bench pad and the cables passing beside it.
Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the hands stop in front of the chest.
progressions: Standing cable chest press (more trunk demand).
Slower return with a pause at the chest.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover: pushes the arm forward and across. The unstable dumbbell press activated the pectoralis about as much as the barbell press in one study (Saeterbakken 2011); seated, more of the effort goes to the chest and arms than to balance.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover: pushes the arm forward and across. The unstable dumbbell press activated the pectoralis about as much as the barbell press in one study (Saeterbakken 2011); seated, more of the effort goes to the chest and arms than to balance.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall on the bench against the cables pulling backward; less demand than standing (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Controls the elbow on the return.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Controls the elbow on the return.
